A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniGEM, with matching core methods, experiments, and theoretical analyses. All 22 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable. Relocated material, equations, tables, and figures can be reliably matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original molecular generation and property prediction experiments on QM9 and GEOM-Drugs, error comparisons, and ablations in Tables 1–6 and Figure 2.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds experiments on BFN-based generation, property-conditioned generation, denoising pre-training comparisons, and shared-layer sensitivity.

M1.justification: The original two-phase architecture and losses remain. Appendix B.1 adds a variant replacing EDM coordinate generation with BFN, while B.2 introduces conditional sampling with a property-loss gradient using the existing prediction head. These substantially extend the generation and inference procedures.

E1.justification: V2 adds property-conditioned molecular generation across six QM9 properties, extending the original unconditional generation and property prediction tasks. The new Frad comparison also includes pre-training on 3.4 million PCQMv2 molecules. UniGEM's original QM9 and GEOM-Drugs coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The original comparator sets remain. Table 7 adds EquiFM, GFMDiff, and GeoBFN to generation comparisons; Table 8 evaluates conditional EDM; Table 9 adds Uni-MOL and Frad with EGNN and TorchMD-NET backbones. These substantially broaden the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: New protocols include conditional-generation evaluation using average MAE, molecular stability, and stable-molecule MAE, plus an EGNN-matched Frad comparison. Appendix C also reports four GEOM-Drugs layers and batches of 32 per GPU, versus v1's nine layers and batch 64. V2's main text retains the earlier settings, creating a reporting conflict rather than establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The original loss, sampling, and nucleation-time ablations remain. V2 adds a shared-layer sensitivity study at depths 1, 3, and 5, an EGNN-matched Frad representation analysis, and illustrative generation trajectories in Figure 5. These are focused additions to the existing analyses.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains the same parenthetical quantities. V2 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or new uncertainty-reporting practice; its additional tables report point estimates.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1–6 retain their scores. New results include 93.7% molecular stability for the BFN variant in Table 7, guided-generation LUMO MAE of 0.592 versus conditional EDM's 0.606 in Table 8, and Frad comparisons in Table 9. These expand the findings substantially; they are not same-setting improvements over v1's UniGEM results.

T1.justification: The existing analyses receive substantive corrections: generation bounds replace q(yT) with q(y0) in prior-error terms and replace second-moment factors with their square roots. Appendix G.3 revises the KL decomposition using a conditional distribution, and F.3 adds the parameter-independent constant linking denoising and score losses. No new theoretical framework is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction narrow the novelty claim from the first unified model to the first diffusion-based unified model. The central claims about two-phase unification and improved generation and prediction remain, while the conclusion retains the broader original novelty wording.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations of conditional-evaluation failures from invalid molecules receiving plausible predicted properties, distinctions from denoising pre-training, and comparability limits arising from different bond-inference rules. It also removes v1's explicit qualification that comparing error upper bounds may not reflect actual performance. The original mechanism interpretations largely remain.

D1.justification: New Appendix C consolidates hyperparameters and adds nucleation-time selection guidance, dataset-specific configuration details, and hardware/runtime disclosures: approximately seven days on one A100 for QM9 and 6.5 days on four A100s for GEOM-Drugs. The conflicting GEOM-Drugs settings limit the reproducibility benefit.

R1.justification: V2 expands positioning relative to denoising pre-training and generators using different bond representations and evaluation rules. Most related work is retained. The GeoBFN reference to Song et al. (2023) disappears, with unresolved citation marks replacing it; several new positioning passages also contain unresolved citations.

P1.justification: V2 condenses Section 2.2, moves property-prediction results into their corresponding subsection, and inserts supplementary-experiment and hyperparameter appendices before the retained material. It also updates affiliations, publication headers, and acknowledgements. Most prose and the main narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the empirical displays with a generation-trajectory figure and Tables 7–10 covering new comparisons, conditional generation, and hyperparameters. Tables 2–3 gain baseline shading and annotated gains, and Table 3 becomes full-width. Existing schematics remain; the former Figure 5 becomes Figure 6.

improvement.justification: Appendices B.1–B.3 provide useful additional evidence for generator adaptability, conditional use, and representation learning, while Appendix C improves practical documentation. These strengthen the paper beyond v1's retained core results. The net gain is limited by inconsistent GEOM-Drugs settings, incompletely specified conditional sampling, and newly unresolved citations.
